summary: DroZon Sprint 1 retest (iteration 2). All 3 previous backend bugs are confirmed FIXED. Backend regression suite is 30/30 green. Frontend E2E: observer launch + observer-banner + hud-logout + auth-gate flows all pass. NEW CRITICAL bug discovered: `POST /api/auth/register` unconditionally sets access/refresh cookies on the response, so when a commander creates another user via UserAdmin.jsx the commander's own session is silently overwritten with the newly-created user's cookies and the follow-up GET /api/users returns 403. The user IS persisted in DB but the UI list does not refresh and shows an error banner.

critical.issue: Session-hijack bug. When an authenticated commander creates a pilot/commander, the server still calls set_auth_cookies() → overwrites the commander's httpOnly access_token+refresh_token with the newly-created user's tokens. The next request from the same browser tab is now made as the new pilot → GET /api/users returns 403 'Rol insuficient. Necesar: commander'. Fix: only set auth cookies when the register call is a public self-registration (no existing valid access_token in the request). Reproduction: login as commander, POST /api/auth/register {role:pilot} in same browser session, then GET /api/users → 403.

minor.issue: backend/.env sets CORS_ORIGINS=* and server uses allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject credentialed requests when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*'. Currently works only because the app is same-origin. Any future cross-origin caller (mobile/native) will silently drop cookies. Set explicit origin list in prod.
app.on_event('startup')/('shutdown') is deprecated in FastAPI 0.109+. Migrate to lifespan handler.

integration_issues.issue: After clicking CREEAZĂ UTILIZATOR, the new user IS created in DB but the users-table is NOT refreshed and an error 'Rol insuficient. Necesar: commander' appears. Root cause is backend register cookie side-effect (see backend critical bug). Frontend workaround would be to re-login/re-fetch /auth/me after create — but the correct fix is server-side.

action_items: server.py:289-333 register() — do NOT call set_auth_cookies() when the caller is already authenticated (i.e., `tok` is present and valid). Only set cookies for public observer self-registration. Alternative: gate cookie-setting on `if role_wanted == 'observer' and not tok`.
server.py CORS — replace wildcard with explicit origin list in production/preview envs.

Optional frontend hardening (UserAdmin.jsx): after createUser() do a re-login using stored commander creds OR call GET /auth/me to detect if session flipped — but the correct fix is the backend one above.
critical_code_review_comments: register() has a design smell: it doubles as (a) public self-signup and (b) admin-create-user. These two flows have opposite session semantics. Splitting into POST /api/auth/register (public, observer only, sets cookies) and POST /api/users (commander-only admin creation, does NOT touch cookies) would eliminate this class of bug.
Old dead comment/logic assumption still visible in tests: 'register does set cookies for the created user!' — the tests worked around this but the frontend cannot.
Cookies still `secure=False` even though preview URL is HTTPS — should be secure=True when behind HTTPS.
Startup event handlers are deprecated FastAPI API — migrate to lifespan.
drozon.html is 10k+ lines — flagged for future modularisation, not fixed here.

rca_of_the_issue.commander_register_403: server.py register() calls set_auth_cookies(response, access, refresh) at line ~325 for EVERY successful registration, including when the caller is a commander. Browsers apply Set-Cookie headers atomically so the commander's httpOnly access_token/refresh_token get replaced with the newly-created user's tokens. axios' next request (GET /api/users to refresh the list) is now sent as that new user → require_role('commander') rejects it with 403. Reproduction: 1) login commander in browser, 2) navigate /users, 3) submit create-user form with role=pilot, 4) observe 403 in devtools + red banner in UI + no new row. Verify user IS in DB via server-side GET /api/users from a separate curl session (works). Fix: guard set_auth_cookies with `if not tok` (public self-signup path) OR split the endpoint into public /register (observer only) and commander-only /users (POST).
